register: PGF Risk Model companion — clause-level source register
line_note: approx_line / line_range refer to the baseline files; headings and tables may span adjacent lines. Each entry paraphrases or quotes the clause; the PGF file is authoritative.

entries.clause: Residual-risk tier is Low/Medium/High/Critical, the track (a) result after measures via the Section 4 matrix for each harm scenario; the highest scenario tier is the tier of the processing. Track (b) never offsets track (a).
Optional limit on total privacy loss (ε and δ) per source population over the lifetime of its ledger, without calendar reset; may be complemented by an operational cap per period.
G-L runs before any risk decision; failure means stop or redesign; nothing can cure a G-L failure.
Lower likelihood never reduces a Catastrophic scenario below High nor a Significant scenario below Medium; relaxation needs independent evidence and an Executive Management decision.
Track (b) is reported separately and never lowers, offsets or averages track (a).

Unlawful processing outside appetite; Critical not acceptable; High accepted only by one designated Executive Management member after G-36; Medium/Low within delegated authority; optional lifetime ε/δ budget with no calendar reset and optional operational cap.

Four likelihood tiers Low/Medium/High/Near-certain; threat-based for identified processing, PET module for releases; the disclosure indicator is not a probability and failure gates prevail over any average.
Minor / Moderate / Significant / Catastrophic with conceptual descriptions; consent is not a severity factor.
Track (b) four-level scale reported to ERM; does not enter the matrix.
4x4 matrix, rows severity, columns likelihood; severity-led floors; may be made stricter; relaxation only within floors with independent evidence.

entries.section: 4. Mapping of Internal Tiers to GDPR Thresholds
entries.clause: DPIA triage independent of tiers; G-36 evaluated for every DPIA; residual High/Critical is a strong indicator, legal conclusion recorded separately; breach and transfer tests not mapped to tiers.

entries.section: 5. Acceptance Authority, Escalation and Mandatory DPO Advice — table and rules
entries.clause: Low PO; Medium PO with EPPO concurrence; High one named Executive Management member after G-36; Critical not acceptable. G-L first; single decider; no self-concurrence; DPO advises on every DPIA and at Medium and above, never approves.

entries.section: 5. Table of Mandatory DPO Advice and Escalation Triggers
entries.clause: Triggers regardless of tier: PET-module failure; Art. 22 / high-risk AI; non-standard weighting; special categories (Art. 9/10); anonymity conclusion.
v1.0 1 Mar 2026; v2.0 22 Aug 2026 (cumulative budget added); v3.0 adopted 20 Oct 2026, effective 23 Oct 2026 (CPO concurrence for Medium; CRO decides High; lifetime ledger with annual cap).

entries.section: 3. Risk Appetite Statement — cumulative disclosure budget
entries.clause: Retail customer population, privacy unit one customer: lifetime ε ≤ 10.0, δ ≤ 1×10⁻⁵, basic composition unless a tighter compatible accountant is documented; no calendar reset; annual pacing cap ε ≤ 7.0 of new spending; warning 80%; at 26 Oct 2026 δ ≈ 8.0×10⁻⁶ reached the warning level. Illustrative parameters.
PanEuropean adopts the template matrix without relaxation; rationale for Significant×Low = Medium and Catastrophic×Low = High.
Worked tier/decision examples including PPI (severity floor applied to Art. 9 data used to decide).

Low PO; Medium PO with CPO concurrence (3 business days, default expiry 12 months); High CRO, 5 business days after G-36 step complete; Critical not acceptable. Where the CPO is the PO, the CRO gives the Medium concurrence.

entries.section: 5. Table of Mandatory Group DPO Advice and Escalation Triggers
entries.clause: PET-module failure; Art. 22 / AI Act; non-standard weight outside 0.5–2.0; special categories (Art. 9/10) even at Low; anonymity conclusion.
Category 3 special category (Art. 9); category 4 criminal-offence data (Art. 10) is not a special category; enhanced regime applies to both.
Credit-scoring data and anti-fraud features Restricted; fraud-case records Restricted / Art. 10; transactional data Confidential.
Lawfulness first; two tracks never offset; numbers are evidence, not a legal safe harbour.

entries.section: Glossary — failure gate, disclosure indicator, privacy unit, harm scenario
entries.clause: Failure gate; disclosure indicator is an uncalibrated ordinal summary, not a probability; privacy unit.

entries.section: 2.1 Position in the Decision Sequence: Gates
entries.clause: Order 1 G-L, 2 G-DPIA, 3 calculation, 4 G-36 (evaluated for every DPIA; High/Critical strong indicator; legal conclusion separate; elapsed period is not authorisation), 5 acceptance by single decider; G-TIA in addition for transfers; calculations on a G-L-failed state are 'not available for acceptance'.

entries.section: 3.1 Architecture — tracks, seven harm types, archetypes
entries.clause: Two tracks; seven Factor A harm types; threat-based likelihood for identified data; PET module for disclosure scenario of archetypes 2–3; controls act on likelihood; archetypes 1, 2a, 2b, 3, 4.
L1 exposure, L2 threat source, L3 control-effectiveness gap: 0–3; L4 event history 0–2 (no 3); measures count through L3 only where evidenced.
0–3 Low; 4–6 Medium; 7–8 High; 9–11 Near-certain.
The likelihood index is always an integer (sum of integer scores); no weights apply.
Where L3 = 3 against L2 ≥ 2, the level is at least High whatever the index.
Inherent: L3 assessed as 3 (without measures); residual: L3 as evidenced; residual used for the residual tier.
Consent, contract or other legal basis does not reduce likelihood or severity.
Diagnostic metrics on the quasi-identifier view are an input to PET planning, not the likelihood of any harm scenario.

entries.section: 3.3.0 Legal status; periodic re-assessment; per-metric results
entries.clause: Module results are evidence, not a legal safe harbour; anonymity is a contextual Recital 26 conclusion; every metric reported individually; a composite never replaces individual results.

G-M1 mandatory metric outside threshold (unfavourable bound); G-M2 unmitigated feasible disclosure path; G-M3 prohibited attribute (legal Art. 9 vs internal policy); G-M4 DP statement incomplete or ledger/cap exceeded; G-M5 missing/invalid/not assessed → INCOMPLETE, blocks like FAIL. FAIL → as-proposed High; reproduced failure → Near-certain (internal routing); not available for acceptance.

0 = no-disclosure baseline, 1 = threshold; rate: v/t; signed advantage: max(0,v)/t; balanced accuracy: |a−0.5|/(t−0.5); AUC likewise; similarity ratio: (1−v)/(1−t); unbounded distance: t/v (v = 0 is a G-M2 qualitative path); ε, δ not normalised. Threshold at/beyond baseline → INCOMPLETE; out-of-domain value → invalid; default exclusive thresholds; weights non-negative summing to 1.
Indicator = Σ normalised × weight; not a probability; translated only for PASS: < 0.5 Low; 0.5–1.0 Medium; INCOMPLETE not assessed; FAIL High; FAIL reproduced Near-certain.

entries.section: 3.3.0 Uncertainty and interval methods; boundary check table
entries.clause: 95% CI; gate uses unfavourable bound (upper for lower-is-safer, lower for higher-is-safer; orientation-invariant for accuracy/AUC; max(0, upper) for signed advantages); Wilson for proportions, bootstrap percentile otherwise; illustrative bounds labelled; boundary examples for threshold 0.60.
Default thresholds are organisation-set illustrative values, not normative.
SDC gates: minimum cell size, dominance, differencing, reconstruction, record-level battery, prohibited attribute.

Privacy unit, adjacency, mechanism and accountant, ε and δ (δ not a failure probability), composition including failed observable runs, output access, implementation assurance, limits of empirical tests; MIA bound (e^ε+δ)/(1+e^ε) under narrow assumptions, not used in the score.

Lifetime ledger per population and privacy unit; no calendar reset; post-processing not charged; basic composition always valid; later smaller δ does not reduce cumulative δ; overlapping observers composed as one party unless shown separate; operational cap never replaces lifetime ledger; every observable output charged, commit-only not adopted without analysis; exceeding budget or cap fails G-M4.
Point scale is ordinal; adding ordinal scores is a structured aid to judgement, not a measurement; band cut-points reviewed with a sensitivity analysis.
Factor A tag; B, C, D, E, G summed; F track (b) only; organisation may add factors but may not remove harm types.

At least Significant where (i) identifiable special-category data are disclosed to an unlimited audience or used to make decisions about the person, or (ii) realistic risk of physical harm; weights cannot lower below floor.
A characteristic is scored in one factor only; a PET or control is reflected in likelihood, not as a severity discount.
Seven harm-type tags; not a score; relevance statement for each.

entries.section: Factor B — Data Class, age modifier, Special Categories, Vulnerability
entries.clause: Data class Public 0 / Internal 1 / Confidential 2 / Restricted 3; age −1 for stale currency-dependent data (not for special categories or permanent attributes; never for synthetic data); special categories (Art. 9) and criminal-offence data (Art. 10) +2; vulnerability 0 / +1 / +2 (children).

entries.section: Factor C — Number of Affected Data Subjects, Source Aggregation, Pilot Restriction
entries.clause: < 100: 0; 100–9,999: 1; 10,000–999,999: 2; ≥ 1,000,000: 3; aggregation of two or more independent sources +1; pilots no separate discount.
Within organisation 0; shared with partner/processor/recipient +1; open unconditional publication +2; recipient control quality is L3, not severity.
+2 where the harm is produced through an Art. 22 decision (incl. determining score, C-634/21) or corrupted data feeding one; not for pure disclosure.
Regime +1/0; financial/operational 0–3; reputational 0–3; sandbox −1 (track (b) only); index = max(0, sum); 0–1 Minor, 2–3 Moderate, 4–5 Significant, ≥ 6 Catastrophic.

entries.section: Factor G — Data Provenance and Reasonable Expectations
entries.clause: Direct clear notice 0; vague purpose +1; third party expected 0; outside expectations +1; scraping same context +1; recontextualised +2; non-identifiable 0; no notice/basis → G-L gate; unattributed → calculation gate.
Maxima follow from the tables: B 7, C 4, D 2, E 2, G 2; no further caps.
Utility metrics are reported separately and may not compensate for privacy risk.

Archetype; G-L record; scenarios; adversary profile; mandatory vs diagnostic metrics; G-M2 definitions; DP statement; weight vector default (1,1,1,1,1), corridor 0.5–2.0, outside corridor EPPO approval + DPO advice; diagnostic alert mode (never for mandatory metrics); provenance attribution gate.
Step 1 per-metric results with CI; Step 2 failure gates prevail; Step 3 normalisation; Step 4 weighting (category × within-category); Step 5 indicator; Step 6 likelihood level.
Severity index = w_B·B + w_C·C + w_D·D + w_E·E + w_G·G, floor 0; A tag; F separate.

entries.section: 4.3 Severity — Step 3 table and contiguity note
entries.clause: < 3.5 Minor; 3.5 to < 6.5 Moderate; 6.5 to < 8.5 Significant; ≥ 8.5 Catastrophic; contiguous, no rounding; default-weight bands 0–3, 4–6, 7–8, ≥ 9; floors then apply.

entries.section: 4.4 Final Residual Risk Level and Decision Steps
entries.clause: Step 0 G-L; 1 likelihood; 2 severity after floors; 3 matrix (inherent and residual); 4 PET outcome (failed → not available for acceptance); 5 highest residual scenario tier; 6 project rules may only be stricter; 7 G-36; 8 acceptance; 9 track (b). Scenarios never averaged.
Blocks 0–4; missing mandatory element is a declared gap, not a silent default; configuration versions retained; anonymity conclusion is a separate legal conclusion.
Defaults not retroactive; calculation obsolete on material change; decision on an obsolete calculation not valid for the changed case.
Bank-specific anchors for L1–L4; bands, override and inherent/residual as Part A.

entries.section: 3.2 proxy metrics and attack battery defaults
entries.clause: Illustrative default thresholds (singling out < 1%, det. linkage < 1%, FS precision@100 < 5%, k-NN < 10%, ZCAP < 0.10, info gain < 0.30, ML inference < 0.10).

≥ 5,000 records per class, five repetitions, 95% CI; unacceptable level = metric threshold unless stated; qualitative paths DCR = 0 and cell attributing a sensitive value to < 10 persons; G-M3 internal policy excludes special-category attributes from open releases.
MIA accuracy < 60%; AUC < 0.60; TPR@FPR0.1% ≤ 1.0% (gate only); DCR P5 ≥ holdout; NNDR > 0.70; linkability and inference advantage ≤ 0.05 (gate only); ε ≤ 3.0 default; δ by project.

Declared inputs and Art. 10 boundary; ε ≤ 3.0 across all rounds; secure aggregation required; MIA AUC < 0.60; gradient-reconstruction test not applicable for observers in scope, INCOMPLETE fallback if secure aggregation lapses.
Min cell ≥ 10; differencing none below 10; reconstruction ≤ 1%; battery at project thresholds; prohibited attribute internal policy; table outside scope → INCOMPLETE (G-M5).
Person-level unit, add/remove adjacency, δ ≤ 1/(100·n) heuristic; MIA bound for information only.
Lifetime ledger, no calendar reset; every run including failed/cancelled observable runs; basic composition; all observers composed as one party; exceeding budget or annual cap fails G-M4.

entries.section: 3.4 Factor B — Special Categories of Data (Art. 9 and Art. 10)
entries.clause: Modifier covers Art. 9 and Art. 10 data; fraud-case records and PSI matches are criminal-offence data; +2 when present.
Project 2 metrics, weights (membership 0.50, memorisation 0.50), thresholds (ε ≤ 2.0, δ 1×10⁻⁹), G-M2 definitions, normalisation formulas, S2 threat-based 1/1/0(3)/1.
S1, S2 severity 3+0+0+3+1+0+0+0 = 7 Significant; track (b) regime +1.
SDC gates; weights singling out 0.20, linkability 0.50 (equal shares), inference 0.30; singling-out threshold 0.5%; G-M2 definitions; table outside scope → G-M5.
S1 severity 3+0+3+0+2+0+0 = 8 Significant.

entries.section: Appendix to Part B — matrix, rounding note, chronology
entries.clause: Matrix reproduced; contributions rounded to three decimals, indicators summed from unrounded contributions; decisions apply authority in force from 23 Oct 2026; earlier decisions under authority then in force.
Audit sample: likelihood 4 Medium / inherent 6; diagnostics indicator 0.857 (not likelihood); severity 3 Minor; Low.
G-L failed as found; calculation documents as-found state; 'G-L failed — not available for acceptance'.
ε 2.1 > 2.0 (G-M1) and δ 8×10⁻⁶ ≠ configured (G-M4) → FAIL despite indicator 0.656; as-proposed High; run charged to ledger because output observed.
All gates pass on unfavourable bounds; indicator 0.537 → Medium; ledger ε 6.5, δ ≈ 8.0×10⁻⁶ by basic composition; S1 Medium, S2 Medium; track (a) Medium; track (b) Moderate.
All gates fail; reproduced → Near-certain; indicator 1.441; ledger would reach ε 10.3, δ ≈ 2.4×10⁻⁵ (G-M4).
SDC gates pass; battery passes on upper bounds; indicator 0.363 → Low; Low × Significant = Medium; anonymity conclusion separate.
SDC and linkage failures; reconstruction reproduced → Near-certain; indicator 1.203; High not available for acceptance.
G-L failed on four facts; release blocked; G-M5 and G-M3 also apply; indicator 0.100; severity for information 10 Catastrophic.
S1 severity 9 Catastrophic, residual Medium → High; inherent Near-certain → Critical (not a decision point).

entries.section: 3.1 Statutory and Supervisory Triggers (WP248 nine criteria)
entries.clause: Art. 35(1), 35(3), Art. 35(4) lists, nine WP248 criteria with two-or-more presumption.

G-36 evaluated for every DPIA; statutory test independent of internal tiers; High/Critical strong indicator; legal conclusion recorded separately by Legal with DPO advice; stricter internal routing labelled; elapsed period is not authorisation.
Single decider after G-36 (after consultation where met); Critical not acceptable; DPO does not approve.

Legal & Compliance records G-36; where met the bank consults the HBDI before processing; CRO decides on consultation; internal policy routes every residual High to consultation unless General Counsel records reasons; decision after G-36 step: Low PO, Medium PO + CPO, High CRO, Critical not acceptable.
Decisions before 23 Oct 2026 taken under the authority then in force; conditional acceptances re-assessed under v3.0 at expiry or next material change.
Status at 26 Oct 2026 for six DPIAs, including DPIA-PSI-01 High, G-36 met, decision pending, sessions paused; DPIA-FL-01 Medium accepted with conditions.
Triage, G-L (Art. 10 for PSI; declared-input boundary for FL), risk assessment with scores, DPO advice, G-36 and decisions (historical and current).
G-TIA outcome is pass or fail; it is not a risk tier.
Informative severity of matched list disclosure: Restricted 3 + criminal-offence data 2 + scale 2 + reach 1 = 8 Significant (corrected 26 Oct 2026).
Inherent: tier without measures (L3 max; PET module as proposed); residual: after implemented and evidenced measures, the decision basis; target: planned tier and date; conditional acceptance.

entries.section: 2. Scope — G-L failures and failed G-TIA never accepted
entries.clause: A G-L failure is a compliance issue, never 'accepted'; a failed G-TIA is 'Suspended' or 'Not accepted'.
Open — decision pending; In treatment; Accepted — conditional (expiry); Accepted; Not accepted — stopped or redesign; Suspended; Closed.
Re-assessment on expiry or material change; changed calculation method not retroactive.
Inherent → residual (target), track (b), decision and status for each record at 26 Oct 2026.
Inherent High, residual High, target Medium (L3 1→0), track (b) Moderate, decision pending CRO, superseded acceptance of 25 Mar 2026, status Open — decision pending, sessions paused.
Lifetime limit ε ≤ 10.0 and δ ≤ 1×10⁻⁵; pacing cap ε ≤ 7.0 per calendar year; warning at 80% of either lifetime limit (template definition at line 171; High alert at line 649).
Ledger ε 6.5 (65%), δ ≈ 8.0×10⁻⁶ (80%) — warning level reached; driven by the failed first generator run that remains in the ledger.
